decisions.reason: The filler-image rule addresses white-space correction on article pages and does not change the already completed template-creation requirement.
Adding subject-relevant filler images does not alter author names, author-photo identity, source, or placement.
The client selects additional images as the white-space remedy without changing the settled Inter font family or its thicker treatment.
The source message contains a separate branding request already represented by the candidate's message-116 MODIFY; the filler-image decision does not change platform or branding state.
The requested filler images are article-subject imagery and do not change the required shape or size of author photos.
Adding images to fill white space does not necessarily change two-page spread behavior, upload format, or page-count parity.
The filler-image quantity and relevance rules do not alter category labels, category mappings, sources, style, or placement.
The white-space correction does not change the prohibition on red in the Dorian Vale article or the reservation of red for the cover.
The source decision concerns imagery on pages with excessive white space and does not add, remove, or reposition the required cover-mentioned articles.
The filler-image rule does not change the tribute page content or its placement toward the end of the magazine.

The general assembly requirement already includes supplied images; the new quantity and relevance constraints belong specifically to balanced article endings and should not be duplicated under the broad assembly requirement.
The image additions may be part of finalizing pages, but they do not change the requirement to complete the table of contents from finalized pagination.
